transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Aurora - Head of ML), Sofia Ramirez (Aurora - DevOps), Evan Brooks (Aurora - Procurement)

Summary:
Quick POC kickoff focused on sizing and success criteria for a timeboxed pilot, commercial guardrails (credits, pilot length, acceptance criteria), and the procurement path if metrics are met. Agreed high-level runbook: 6-week pilot, initial credits suggested $30k, benchmark targets: 99th pct latency < 350ms for short chat workloads, 1.2k sustained req/sec for the generation endpoint, quality threshold 92% pass on labeled eval set. Redwood to share pilot terms and seed sandbox model; SE to run throughput test with Aurora sample dataset next week.

Topics covered:
- Pilot commercial guardrails (credits, expiry, overage)
- Success criteria and quantitative benchmarks (latency, throughput, quality)
- Workload sizing and representative prompts
- Required infra and private vs hosted tradeoffs
- Procurement steps and timelines (LOI/SOW/PO)

Action items (summary):
- Seed sandbox + run initial benchmark (Redwood SE)
- Pilot credit summary + T&Cs (AE)
- Procurement timing + PO contact (Aurora procurement)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Okay, good afternoon uh — good morning for some, but hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marcus Li: Marcus here.
[00:09] Sofia Ramirez: Sofia on DevOps.
[00:11] Evan Brooks: Evan from procurement.
[00:13] Priya Nandakumar: Priya from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Jamie Ortega: Cool. So the agenda is twofold: one, make sure we agree on what success looks like for a 4-6 week pilot and two, commercial guardrails — credits, term, path to procurement. Sound good?
[00:30] Marcus Li: Yep that's exactly what we need. We're trying to validate cost and perf for a chat augmentation feature, plus make sure any private data concerns are addressed.
[00:42] Priya Nandakumar: Great, do you have a workload shape or traffic profile? Rough numbers help us size the tests — avg tokens per request, concurrency, and acceptable p99.
[00:54] Marcus Li: Sure, rough shape: median payload about 120 tokens, peak concurrent active users around 60 in early tests, but we expect to scale up. For benchmark we'll simulate 500 concurrent sessions hitting the API to emulate production day-one spikes. P99 target ideally under 300-350ms for short turn gen, but if that's unrealistic we'll accept up to 400ms as a backstop.
[01:18] Jamie Ortega: That helps. For pilot guardrails on the commercial side we typically offer timeboxed credits usable across hosted endpoints. For a test like this we'd recommend $25-35k in credits depending on how many iterations you want to run. Credits expire at pilot end unless we roll into purchase. Any constraints from your side?
[01:38] Evan Brooks: From procurement we prefer a clear SOW or MSA before any invoice, but for pilots small credits are OK under an MSA addendum. We need the T&Cs and a contact person for the procurement team.
[01:52] Jamie Ortega: Understood. I'll send the pilot term sheet with anchor pricing and the template addendum. Our standard is 6 weeks, can be shortened to 4 if you want a tighter run.
[02:03] Marcus Li: One question: do credits cover private deployment? We might prefer VPC for data residency.
[02:11] Priya Nandakumar: Good question — pilot credits usually apply to hosted Redwood API. For Redwood Private there's an on-prem or dedicated option that sometimes needs a separate contract and a small infra fee. We can do a hosted pilot with strict retention + KMS, or spin up a temporary dedicated pool if you need isolated GPUs. There's a bit of lead time for dedicated.
[02:33] Sofia Ramirez: How much lead time are we talking? If we need dedicated for compliance, can that be within the pilot window?
[02:39] Priya Nandakumar: Typically 2-4 weeks to provision a dedicated pool if we have capacity. If tight, start with hosted pilot and we can migrate to a dedicated node during week two as we confirm performance — though that complicates the benchmark baseline.
[02:55] Marcus Li: Okay makes sense. For success criteria we want both perf and quality checks. Perf: p99 under 350ms for single-turn chat at median tokens, throughput at least 1.0k req/sec sustained for a 5-minute window. Quality: automated eval against 10k labelled prompts with at least 92% pass on correctness and no more than 3% hallucination rate on the held-out set.
[03:22] Priya Nandakumar: Helpful to have concrete numbers. For throughput we'll need sample prompts and realistic token distribution. Also let us know how you measure hallucinations — do you have rubric or do you want Redwood's eval harness?
[03:36] Marcus Li: We have a rubric but might use Redwood's harness to keep things consistent. We'll share the eval set as CSV and a scoring script.
[03:43] Jamie Ortega: Great — include a short README for the scripts. We'll run both Redwood's eval and your script and reconcile differences.
[03:50] Evan Brooks: About credits — any overage model? If we blow through the pilot credits, how do we handle that?
[03:57] Jamie Ortega: Good point. We typically cap at the credit amount. If you anticipate overruns we can do a pre-authorized overage or pause the pilot and discuss top-up. We'll document that in the pilot T&C.
[04:08] Sofia Ramirez: Also need to confirm security posture: SOC 2, ISO, KMS integration, audit logs, data deletion window.
[04:18] Priya Nandakumar: We are SOC 2 Type II; ISO in progress. KMS integration supported for dedicated/private; hosted supports envelope encryption with managed keys but we can also bring your own keys via KMS. Audit logging and per-token tracing are in the Console. I'll attach the security pack link.
[04:34] Jamie Ortega: Note: link to security pack in chat — https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (shared)
[04:38] Marcus Li: Thanks. On the benchmarking plan — what does Redwood need from our side to size the test?
[04:45] Priya Nandakumar: Ideally: 1) representative prompt templates (10-15) 2) token length distribution histogram 3) expected concurrency profiles (ramp up/ramp down) 4) a small sample dataset of 2k rows to validate quality. Also let us know if you need streaming vs non-streaming responses.
[05:01] Marcus Li: We'll provide that by Friday.
[05:04] Jamie Ortega: For the bench itself, SE will run a baseline on both a quantized and a float model variant so you can see perf/cost tradeoffs. We'll report: tokens/sec, avg latency, p50/p90/p99, and cost per 1M tokens at the observed config.
[05:20] Priya Nandakumar: We'll also show how KV cache and prefix caching helps for conversational use — often reduces 40-60% of compute in our tests for repeated prefixes.
[05:29] Sofia Ramirez: That caching is interesting. Do we need to change our client to use conversation IDs?
[05:34] Priya Nandakumar: Minimal changes — primarily persist conv IDs and allow the API to reuse cached KV state. We'll share a quick code sample.
[05:42] Jamie Ortega: Another commercial note — if pilot metrics are hit, the path to procurement usually follows these steps: LOI -> SOW with committed throughput (if Dedicated) -> negotiation on term and SLA -> PO. Evan, does that align with your process?
[05:56] Evan Brooks: Yes that matches. We'll need estimated MRR/ARR numbers to justify to finance if we move from credits to reserved capacity. Also internal review cycles can take 2-3 weeks.
[06:07] Marcus Li: On timelines: we want to complete pilot and make a decision within 6 weeks so we can budget for Q4.
[06:13] Jamie Ortega: Noted. So proposed pilot timeline: week 0 (this week) - kickoff and data handoff, week 1 - seed sandbox + initial bench, week 2 - run production-like throughput tests and quality evals, week 3-4 - iteration and tuning (quantization/batch configs), week 5 - final acceptance run, week 6 - decision + contracting prep. Does that cadence work?
[06:31] Marcus Li: Yes.
[06:32] [10:02] (short gap in recording noted)
[10:10] Priya Nandakumar: Quick dive on the benchmark details — for the throughput test we'll use a traffic generator that mimics your ramp profile. We'll test three configs: default fp16, 8-bit quantized, and an aggressive batching config. Each run ~10 minutes for steady-state metrics.
[10:29] Marcus Li: For the quality eval, we need to ensure the scoring is deterministic. We'll lock RNG seeds and provide scoring harness.
[10:36] Priya Nandakumar: Good call. On instrumentation we'll enable trace hooks — please share any correlation IDs you use so we can align logs.
[10:44] Sofia Ramirez: About networking: do you support VPC peering and private endpoints?
[10:49] Priya Nandakumar: Yes: private endpoints, VPC peering, and customer-managed subnets for Redwood Private. For hosted we provide TLS and configurable IP allowlists, but peering is only for Private/Dedicated deployments.
[10:59] Evan Brooks: What about egress costs and who pays for them?
[11:03] Jamie Ortega: If we provision Dedicated in your cloud, egress is typically billed to the customer by cloud provider; we can estimate based on expected traffic. For hosted we absorb infrastructure egress under our pricing, except large data exports which we'd discuss case-by-case.
[11:18] Marcus Li: Back to credits — can you do milestone-based credit release? I.e., portion released after initial bench, remainder after acceptance?
[11:25] Jamie Ortega: We can structure it that way — 50% on seed + 50% on final acceptance is common. We'll put that in the T&C.
[11:32] Marcus Li: Great. Any red flags on Redwood side?
[11:34] Priya Nandakumar: Biggest risk is trying to migrate to a dedicated pool mid-pilot — that can introduce variability in baseline numbers. Also ensure your eval set covers edge-case prompts to capture hallucination failure modes.
[11:47] Sofia Ramirez: Understood.
[11:49] [15:00] (noise, someone shuffling papers)
[15:05] Jamie Ortega: Logistics — I'll attach three docs: pilot term sheet, security pack, and benchmark runbook. Links I'll drop in the follow-up email.
[15:14] Evan Brooks: Send to procurement@aurora-tech.com and cc legal.
[15:18] Jamie Ortega: Will do.
[15:20] Marcus Li: On measurement — can Redwood provide per-route dashboards for the pilot? We want token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model variant.
[15:29] Priya Nandakumar: Yes, Console shows per-route/per-model token breakdowns, cost estimation, and latency percentiles. We'll grant you access to the pilot org.
[15:36] Marcus Li: Perfect.
[15:38] [20:00] (short tangent about other vendors)
[20:25] Marcus Li: We evaluated vendor X but their quantization story was weak. Redwood's caching + quantization combo is attractive if it holds up.
[20:35] Jamie Ortega: Cool — we'll make sure the bench demonstrates that synergy.
[20:39] Sofia Ramirez: One more ops question — during bench runs do you throttle retries/backoff or do you expect the client to handle it?
[20:47] Priya Nandakumar: We emulate client behavior but recommend your client implement exponential backoff to avoid sharp thundering-herd retries. For load tests we run with no artificial retries to measure raw capacity.
[20:58] Marcus Li: Okay.
[21:00] Jamie Ortega: Alright, quick recap and owners: 1) Redwood SE (Priya) to provision sandbox and run first bench by 2025-08-22; 2) Redwood AE (Jamie) to share pilot credit T&Cs by 2025-08-20; 3) Aurora (Evan) to provide procurement contact and PO timing by 2025-08-25; 4) Aurora (Marcus) to share prompts, token histogram, and eval set by 2025-08-22.
[21:30] Marcus Li: Yep I have those noted.
[21:33] Evan Brooks: Timeline sounds fine. We'll start internal approvals this week.
[21:36] Jamie Ortega: I'll schedule the follow-up bench sync for next Tuesday 16:00 UTC. Does that work for everyone?
[21:43] Sofia Ramirez: Works for me.
[21:44] Marcus Li: Works.
[21:45] Priya Nandakumar: Works.
[21:46] Jamie Ortega: Great. Any last questions?
[21:48] Marcus Li: None from me.
[21:49] Evan Brooks: All good.
[21:50] Jamie Ortega: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and the sandbox invite.
[21:55] (meeting ends)
